children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 17, with oil prices falling further as additional Saudi crude supplies eased concerns over Middle East disruptions. Gold remained under pressure after the Federal Reserve raised rates and signalled another hike could come before year-end.

Oil prices fell in early trade on Thursday, extending the previous day's losses, as reports of Saudi Arabia offering extra crude cargoes through Oman reduced fears of supply disruptions in the Middle East.
Brent crude futures dropped $1.24, or 1.2%, to $104.59 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were down $1.14, or 1.1%, at $101.29. Both contracts fell about $3 on Wednesday.
In precious metals, gold held a decline after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years
and signaled another hike was likely before year-end.
Bullion was trading around $4,270 an ounce, after falling 2% over the previous three sessions as traders priced in the Fed’s widely expected move.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously late Wednesday to increase the benchmark federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point. Its median outlook for rates at the end of 2026 was 4.1%, up from 3.8% earlier, indicating support for more hikes.
Silver rose 0.5% to $63.28 an ounce. Platinum and palladium edged higher.

The dollar held onto Wednesday’s gains after the US central bank raised interest rates and signaled more are coming. The dollar Spot index stands pat after gaining 0.5% on Wednesday to hit a one-month high. US 10-year yields dropped 2bps to 4.99%.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil extends losses, gold under pressure
